mainTopic: Why רב זביד rejects רב פפא's reading of the משנה, and the scope and reason of רב's rule of מעמד שלשתן
overview: Earlier the גמרא offered two ways to explain our משנה so that it does not clash with רב's rule of מעמד שלשתן. First it explains that רב פפא holds רב's rule works for a loan and a deposit alike. Then it asks why רב זביד did not follow רב פפא. רב זביד answers that the משנה cannot be about a שכיב מרע, because the משנה requires the man to say 'give', while a dying man's 'write' is enough. To support this, the גמרא quotes a משנה listing people in danger whose 'write' counts, ending with רבי שמעון שזורי, who adds the מסוכן. רב אשי rejects the proof, since our משנה may follow the רבנן, who leave the sick man off the list. Next the גמרא studies רב's rule itself. רבא first limits it to a deposit, then swears that רב meant it even for a loan, and שמואל in the name of לוי agrees. אמימר explains the rule as an obligation the borrower took on when the loan was made. רב אשי disproves this from people born after the loan, and he begins his own explanation, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב פפא holds רב's rule covers loans and deposits alike
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רב פפא did not follow רב זביד: in רב פפא's view, רב's rule applies equally to a loan and to a deposit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא holds that when רב said his rule, it makes no difference whether it is a loan or a deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question asked just before this point: why didn't רב פפא explain the משנה the way רב זביד did? The answer is that רב פפא understands רב's rule to work for both a loan and a deposit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule is that a transfer of money made in the presence of all three people (מעמד שלשתן) takes effect. If that rule covers a deposit just as it covers a loan, then explaining the משנה by splitting loans from deposits does not avoid the contradiction. So רב פפא needed a different explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds / he is of the opinion
there is no difference
a loan, where the borrower owes a sum of money but not specific coins
a deposit, where specific money or items are held for someone

phrases.english: Rav Pappa holds
that when Rav said [his rule],
phrases.notes: רב's rule is the one discussed earlier on the daf: a transfer of money said in front of all three people works.

phrases.english: it makes no difference whether it is a loan
and it makes no difference whether it is a deposit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from just before this section about why רב פפא did not adopt רב זביד's explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפא holds that רב's rule of מעמד שלשתן applies to both a loan and a deposit, so an explanation that depends on telling the two apart does not work for him.

steps.title: Why didn't רב זביד follow רב פפא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question around and asks why רב זביד did not explain the משנה the way רב פפא did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד: what is the reason he did not say like רב פפא?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the reverse question about the other אמורא. This line sets up the next move, where we will hear רב זביד's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's explanation treats the משנה as a case of a שכיב מרע. The גמרא wants to know what was wrong with that in רב זביד's eyes.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?
did not say in line with (someone else's view)

phrases.english: Rav Zevid, what is the reason
that he did not say like Rav Pappa?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב זְבִיד מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the previous question by asking the same thing about the other אמורא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What objection did רב זביד have to רב פפא's explanation of the משנה?

steps.title: The משנה cannot be about a שכיב מרע
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד's reason is that the משנה cannot be explained as a case of a שכיב מרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה cannot be explained as being about a deathbed patient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב זביד's reason: our משנה cannot be talking about a שכיב מרע. Since רב פפא's explanation needs that setting, רב זביד could not use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is only the claim. The proof that the משנה is not about a שכיב מרע comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: can be established / explained as (referring to a certain case)
our משנה
a person who is seriously ill and may be dying (a deathbed patient)

phrases.english: The mishna cannot be established
as dealing with a deathbed patient.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב זביד holds that the משנה cannot be about a שכיב מרע, so רב פפא's explanation fails for him.

steps.title: Proof from the גט case in the same משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know this, and points to the line in our משנה: if someone says 'give this גט to my wife' and then dies, it is not given after his death.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know? From what it teaches: 'One who says: Give this גט to my wife, and this שטר שחרור to my slave,' and he died, they should not give it after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for רב זביד's claim. It quotes the line about a גט and a שטר שחרור from the same משנה, which will be the basis of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By itself this line only says a גט is not given after the husband dies. The proof comes from reading closely what the line implies, which the גמרא does in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: from where (do we know this)?
from the fact that it teaches
give!
a document that frees a slave

phrases.english: From where [do we know this]?
From the fact that it teaches:
"One who says: Give this bill of divorce to my wife
and this document of freedom to my slave,"
and he died –
they should not give it after death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to prove the claim made in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה is not about a שכיב מרע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The line in our משנה: 'האומר תנו גט זה לאשתי... ומת לא יתנו לאחר מיתה.'

steps.title: Reading the משנה closely: 'give' is required, but not for a שכיב מרע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws two implications from the משנה: during his life the גט is given, but only because he said 'give.' A שכיב מרע, though, has his גט given even without saying 'give.' So the משנה cannot be about a שכיב מרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that he died; but during his life, they give it. The reason is that he said 'give'; but if he didn't say 'give,' they do not give it. Yet for a deathbed patient, even if he didn't say 'give,' they give it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely. It shows that the משנה's ruling depends on the man having said 'give,' which would not matter for a שכיב מרע. That shows the משנה is about a healthy person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Implication one: the only problem was that he died, so while he is alive the גט is given. Implication two: that works only because he said 'give,' so 'write' alone would not be enough. A שכיב מרע's 'write' is enough even without 'give,' so the משנה must be speaking about a healthy man.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason is because... (used to point out an implication)
but (in the opposite case)...
while he is alive
even though

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה makes the giving of the גט depend on the word 'give.' A שכיב מרע doesn't need that word, so רב זביד concludes the משנה is about a healthy person and cannot be explained like רב פפא.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof doesn't come from the words 'he died.' It comes from the hidden implication that saying 'give' is required. That requirement only makes sense for a healthy person.

phrases.english: The reason is that he died,
but while he is alive – they give it;
the reason is that he said "give,"
but if he did not say "give," they do not give it;
phrases.notes: He means a man who only said 'write a גט' and never told them to give it.

phrases.english: yet a deathbed patient –
even though he did not say "give,"
they give it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the implications from the line quoted in step 4 to finish the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה is about a healthy person, not a שכיב מרע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implication of the משנה that 'give' is required, compared with the rule that a שכיב מרע's 'write' is enough.

steps.title: Source: people in danger whose 'write' counts as 'give'
steps.stepSummary: To support the idea that some people's 'write' is enough, the גמרא quotes a משנה. A man led out to execution who says 'write a גט' has it written and given. Later this was extended to someone setting sail or leaving in a caravan.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: At first they would say: One who is led out in a קולר and said 'Write a גט for my wife' — these should write and give it. They then said: even one who sets sail and one who leaves in a caravan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins bringing a source for the rule that a person in danger only needs to say 'write.' This source sets up the point about a שכיב מרע, which the משנה continues to develop right after these lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healthy man's 'write' does not mean 'give.' For a man facing death, though, we assume he wants the גט given, so 'write' is enough. The list of such people grows from the condemned man to travelers facing danger, and this supports treating a שכיב מרע the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה
at first / originally
a neck chain put on someone led out to execution
write!
one who sets out to sea
a caravan traveling through dangerous land

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
At first they would say:
One who is led out in a neck chain [to be executed],
and said "Write a bill of divorce for my wife" –
these people should write and give it.
They then said,
even one who sets sail and one who leaves in a caravan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind step 5's claim that a שכיב מרע's 'write' is enough.
steps.raayaObject: That for a person in danger of dying, saying 'write' is treated as if he said 'give.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about one led out in a קולר, then extended to one setting sail or leaving in a caravan.

steps.title: רבי שמעון שזורי adds a person in danger of dying
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה ends with רבי שמעון שזורי, who says a מסוכן also only needs to say 'write'. This completes the proof that our משנה is not about a שכיב מרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון שזורי says: even a person who is dangerously ill (his 'write' is enough).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה from step 6. רבי שמעון שזורי adds a dangerously ill person to the list of people whose 'write' is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מסוכן is a שכיב מרע. If saying 'write' is enough for him, he certainly does not need to say 'give'. Our משנה needs the man to say 'give', so it cannot be talking about a שכיב מרע.

keyTerms.meaning: A person in danger of dying, which is the same as a שכיב מרע
Even / also
The תנא who adds the dangerously ill person to the list

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says:
Even one who is dangerously ill.
phrases.notes: He means that for this sick man too, saying 'write' is enough, and the גט is written and given.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי אוֹמֵר: אַף הַמְסוּכָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה quoted in step 6, which supplies the key part of the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a שכיב מרע's 'write' is enough, so a משנה that needs 'give' is not about him
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing people whose 'write' is enough, ending with רבי שמעון שזורי

steps.title: רב אשי: maybe our משנה follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges the proof. Only רבי שמעון שזורי says a sick man's 'write' is enough. Our משנה might follow the רבנן, who disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects: Who tells us that our משנה follows רבי שמעון שזורי? Maybe it follows the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the proof for רב זביד's view. The proof works only if our משנה agrees with רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן did not put the מסוכן on the list. In their view, a sick man still has to say 'give'. So our משנה could follow the רבנן and still be talking about a שכיב מרע, and רב פפא's explanation stays possible.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it
And who tells us?
Perhaps
The Sages who disagree with the single opinion

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the משנה must follow the רבנן. He only shows that the proof is not forced, because we do not know whose opinion our משנה follows.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objects to it:
And who tells us
that our Mishnah is Rabbi Shimon Shezuri's view?
Perhaps it is the Rabbis' view!
phrases.notes: The רבנן left the sick man off the list, so for them he still has to say 'give'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof built in steps 4 to 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof that our משנה cannot be about a שכיב מרע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof assumes our משנה follows רבי שמעון שזורי. If it follows the רבנן, a שכיב מרע also needs to say 'give', so the משנה could be about him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This leaves רב פפא's reading of the משנה as a שכיב מרע case still possible.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב זביד's proof (steps 4–7) that our משנה cannot be about a שכיב מרע
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes our משנה follows רבי שמעון שזורי (אף המסוכן). If it follows the רבנן, a שכיב מרע still has to say 'give', so the משנה's need for 'תנו' does not exclude a שכיב מרע.

steps.title: רב's rule: transferring money by speech with all three present
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now studies רב's rule on its own. If someone says 'I have a מנה in your hands, give it to so-and-so', and all three people are present, the third person acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the statement itself: רב הונא said in the name of רב: If someone says, 'You are holding a מנה of mine, give it to so-and-so,' and all three are present, that person acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the word גופא, the גמרא goes back to a statement mentioned earlier and studies it on its own. That statement is רב's rule about passing on money just by speaking, when all three people are present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person needs a formal act of acquisition (a קנין) to get property. Here, speaking in front of all three people is enough to give the money to the third person. This is the rule known as מעמד שלשתן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself': going back to study a statement mentioned earlier
A sum of one hundred זוז
With all three people present
He acquires it
So-and-so

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא – אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
"I have a maneh in your hands,
give it to so-and-so,"
in the presence of all three of them, he acquires it.
phrases.notes: The three are the owner, the one holding the money, and the one receiving it.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא – אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the גט discussion and looks closely at רב's rule, which was mentioned earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Telling the one who holds your money to give it to someone else, with all three present, transfers ownership without a formal act of acquisition.

steps.title: רבא: the rule makes sense only for a deposit
steps.stepSummary: רבא suggests that רב's rule applies to a פקדון but not to a מלוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רב's statement makes sense for a deposit, but not for a loan.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proposes a limit on רב's rule. It would work for a פקדון but not for a מלוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a פקדון, the actual money is sitting there and still belongs to the owner, so he can easily point it to someone else. A loan's money has already been spent, and what is left is only a debt. Passing on a debt just by speaking seems harder.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / it stands to reason
A deposit: an item held for its owner
A loan: money owed as a debt

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rav's statement makes sense with a deposit,
but with a loan, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִילְּתֵיהּ דְּרַב בְּפִקָּדוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the cases that רב's rule covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's rule would apply only to a deposit, not to a loan.

steps.title: רבא swears: רב meant it even for a loan
steps.stepSummary: רבא declares with an oath that רב in fact said his rule even for a מלוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But by God! רב said it even about a loan.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes back the limit he suggested in step 10. He swears that רב's rule covers a loan too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic suggested the rule fits only a deposit, but what רב actually said settles the question. The rule of מעמד שלשתן works even for a debt.

keyTerms.meaning: 'By God!': a strong oath stressing the truth
Even

steps.confusionAlert: This oath does not argue against רב. It rejects the limit from step 10 and shows that רב's rule is broader than רבא first thought.

phrases.english: But by God! Rav said it:
even with a loan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns the limit proposed in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רב's rule is limited to a deposit
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב himself said the rule applies even to a loan.

steps.title: Support from שמואל in the name of לוי: even a loan
steps.stepSummary: A statement of שמואל in the name of לוי says clearly that a מלוה can be passed on with all three present.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught: שמואל said in the name of לוי: If someone says, 'You owe me a loan, give it to so-and-so,' and all three are present, that person acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אמורא's teaching that agrees with רבא's oath. Even a loan can be passed on through מעמד שלשתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי's wording names a מלוה outright, so there is no room to limit the rule to a deposit. This settles the point: speaking in front of all three people passes on even a debt.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught: introduces another source that agrees
In the name of

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of מעמד שלשתן (all three people present) passes on ownership just by speaking. According to רב and לוי it works for both a deposit and a loan.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Shmuel said in the name of Levi:
"I have a loan in your hands,
give it to so-and-so,"
in the presence of all three of them, he acquires it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּלֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 11 with another source that agrees.
steps.raayaObject: That מעמד שלשתן works even for a loan
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל in the name of לוי, who uses the word מלוה outright

steps.title: What is the reason behind רב's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what legal reason makes the transfer in front of all three people work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב's rule works. This short question sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a debt cannot simply be handed over to someone else by speaking. The third person did not lend anything, so the גמרא wants to know what legal reason makes him the new owner of the debt.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
A transfer done with all three people present

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving that רב's rule covers a מלוה, the גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The legal mechanism that lets the third person acquire the debt.

steps.title: אמימר: the borrower obligated himself from the start
steps.stepSummary: אמימר explains that it is as if the borrower said, when he took the loan, 'I am obligated to you and to anyone who comes because of you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: It is as if the borrower said to the lender when he received the money, 'I am obligated to you and to anyone who comes on your behalf.'
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers the question. The borrower's obligation to the third person was already built in when the loan was first given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אמימר, nothing new is created at the moment of transfer. The borrower is understood to have obligated himself from the start to anyone the lender sends. So when the lender points to the third person, that person was already covered by the original promise.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who offers the first explanation
The giving of the money, meaning the moment the loan was made
I am obligated or bound to pay
Because of you, on your behalf

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
It becomes like the borrower saying to the lender
at the time the money was given:
I am obligated to you, to you yourself,
and to anyone who comes because of you.
phrases.notes: The third person the lender later points to counts as 'someone who comes because of you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר: נַעֲשָׂה כְּאוֹמֵר לוֹ בִּשְׁעַת מַתַּן מָעוֹת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The borrower is treated as having obligated himself at the time of the loan to the lender and to anyone the lender sends.

steps.title: רב אשי: what about people not yet born at the time of the loan?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges אמימר. If the obligation began when the loan was made, then a transfer to people born later should fail, because no one can acquire before he exists. Even רבי מאיר agrees to that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: If so, suppose the lender transferred the debt to people who had not yet been born when the money was lent. Would they not acquire it?! Even רבי מאיר, who holds that a person can transfer something that does not yet exist, only says this when the receiver already exists. He agrees that a transfer to someone who does not yet exist is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks אמימר's explanation. He uses the case of a third person who was not yet born when the loan was made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the borrower's obligation began at the moment of the loan, it could only cover people who existed then. Even רבי מאיר, the most lenient view, agrees that you cannot transfer to someone who does not exist. Yet רב said his rule with no limits, so it should work for anyone, including people born later. That means אמימר's reason does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: introduces a problem that follows from the previous explanation
People who will be born later
Something that has not yet come into existence
The תנא who allows transferring something that does not yet exist

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two 'things not in the world.' רבי מאיר allows the OBJECT being given to not exist yet. Here the problem is that the PERSON receiving does not exist yet, and even רבי מאיר does not allow that.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
But if so,
if he transferred it to people who were born later,
phrases.notes: The transfer happens now, in front of all three, but the receivers were born after the loan was made.

phrases.english: who did not exist when the money was given,
would it then also be that they do not acquire?!
For even according to Rabbi Meir,
who says a person can transfer
something that has not yet come into the world,
that applies only when transferring to someone who exists,
phrases.notes: Here 'דבר' means the person receiving, not the item being given.

phrases.english: but to someone who does not yet exist, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's claim that the obligation to the third person began at the time of the loan.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An obligation made at the time of the loan cannot cover people not yet born, since even רבי מאיר forbids transferring to someone who does not exist. Yet רב's general rule would let them acquire, so אמימר's reason cannot be right.

steps.title: רב אשי begins his own explanation
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting אמימר's reason, רב אשי introduces his own explanation of רב's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. רב אשי is about to give a different reason for רב's rule, and the content continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that the previous explanation has been dropped. רב אשי needs a reason that works even for people born after the loan, so his answer will not depend on an obligation from the time of the loan.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the earlier approach and offers a new one

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אמימר's rejected answer with a new answer to the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet stated here. It is only introduced, and the content follows in the continuation of the daf.
